title: Logical Replication Architecture & Wal2json
description: Understand WAL logical decoding, output plugins (wal2json, test_decoding), replication streams, and event-driven architectures.

data.text: Underlying PostgreSQL's logical replication is **Logical Decoding**. The engine reads raw WAL segments and decodes internal binary storage modifications into an application-consumable stream of logical row changes (using plugins like `wal2json` or `pgoutput`).

data.title: Reading Decoded WAL JSON Stream with wal2json
data.content: Consuming database change events directly from a replication slot.

data.text: Logical Decoding and Streaming Change Events

Logical decoding turns the write-ahead log into a stream of row-level changes that an external consumer can read. A replication slot tracks how far the consumer has read; if the consumer stops, the slot holds the WAL it has not yet acknowledged, which is why an abandoned logical slot can bloat the primary's disk.

data.title: Read changes with a logical slot
data.content: The temporary slot exists only for the session. A persistent slot survives disconnects and must be dropped when the consumer is retired.
data.code:
-- Inspect the decoded changes from the built-in test plugin
SELECT *
FROM pg_logical_slot_get_changes(
    'test_slot',
    NULL,
    NULL
);

-- Create and monitor a persistent logical slot
SELECT * FROM pg_create_logical_replication_slot('cdc_slot', 'test_decoding');

SELECT
    slot_name,
    plugin,
    active,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) AS retained_wal
FROM pg_replication_slots;

data.title: Logical slots are a disk risk
data.text: Unlike a physical slot that a live standby keeps current, a logical slot whose consumer is gone retains WAL forever, because the slot cannot know when it is safe to advance. Monitor `pg_replication_slots` for `active = false` with a growing `retained_wal`, alert on it, and set `max_slot_wal_keep_size` so the server can invalidate a runaway slot instead of filling the disk.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Logical decoding extracts clean row changes directly from the Write-Ahead Log.
It introduces near-zero overhead on production transaction execution.
Powers modern real-time data streaming to Elasticsearch, Snowflake, and Apache Kafka.
